This installs the `t3` binary to `~/.local/bin`. If that folder is not on your
`PATH` yet, the installer says so and, for zsh, bash on Linux, and fish, prints
a command to add it. On Windows, `t3` works in the same PowerShell window right
away; add the folder to your `PATH` for new windows. If a `t3` that the
installer or the desktop app did not create is already there, it leaves that
one alone and stops. Set `T3CODE_CHANNEL=nightly` to install the nightly train, or
`T3CODE_VERSION` to pin an exact version.

| Task                                  | Command                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Start the server and open the web app | `t3`                                                                    |
| Start the server without a browser    | `t3 serve`                                                              |
| Use it from your other devices        | `t3 up` ([details](./remote-access.md))                                 |
| Keep it running in the background     | `t3 service install` ([details](./background-service.md))               |
| Move to the newest release            | `t3 update`                                                             |
| Reclaim database space                | `t3 doctor` ([details](./background-service.md#reclaim-database-space)) |
| Remove it again                       | `t3 uninstall`                                                          |

Run `t3 help` or `t3 --help` for the full reference. To start in a new working
directory, use an explicit path such as `t3 ./my-project`. A bare directory name
is accepted only if it already exists.

If `t3` or `t3 start` reports an already running server, connect to that server
instead. Stop it before starting a replacement, or use a different `--base-dir`
for an independent server.

To try T3 Code once without installing it, run `npx t3@latest` instead (needs
Node.js for `npx`). It offers to install the `t3` command first. If you say no,
it asks again at the next minor release, and `npx t3 install` installs it later.
`npx t3` always runs the version npm picked, even when a `t3` is installed. On
the nightly train, run your installed `t3` (for example `t3 connect`), not
`npx t3`, which runs the latest stable release.


## Providers

Open **Settings → Providers** in the web or desktop app, select the environment,
and enable the provider you want. Installation, login, and configuration belong
to that environment's machine, even when you connect from a phone or another
computer.

| Provider    | Install and authenticate                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Codex       | [Connect with ChatGPT](./providers-codex.md#connect-with-chatgpt), or install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`. |
| Claude      | Install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code), then run `claude auth login`.                                                              |
| Cursor      | Install [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli), then run `agent login`.                                                                                     |
| Grok Build  | Install [Grok Build CLI](https://x.ai/cli), then run `grok login`.                                                                                        |
| Kiro        | Install [Kiro CLI](https://kiro.dev/docs/cli/), then run `kiro-cli login`.                                                                                |
| OpenCode    | Install [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai), then run `opencode auth login`.                                                                                  |
| Antigravity | Install and sign in with Google from T3 Code's provider settings.                                                                                         |
| Pi          | Install [Pi](./providers-pi.md#set-up-pi) with Node.js 22.19 or newer, then run `pi` and `/login`.                                                        |
| Muse Code   | Install [Muse Code](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code) on the server, run `muse login`, then enable it in Settings → Providers.                          |
| fx          | Install [fx](https://fx.sh) with `curl -fsSL https://fx.sh/setup.sh \| bash`, then run `fx login`.                                                        |

Provider CLIs must be on the server's `PATH`. If T3 Code cannot find one, set its
**Binary path** in provider settings, especially when using a version manager.
Cursor's executable is `cursor-agent`, although its login command is
`agent login`. Codex connected through ChatGPT and Antigravity can use their
managed runtimes without a `PATH` entry.

T3 Code warns when a provider version has known compatibility problems with your
release. Check **Settings → Providers** on that environment for the recommended
version or range. When its package manager supports installing a specific version,
you can install the recommendation there. Otherwise use the provider's installer
on the environment's machine. An unlisted version is unverified.

When a provider CLI is behind its latest release, its provider card shows the
available version. **Update now** runs the installer that owns the CLI
(Homebrew, mise, or a global npm, pnpm, Yarn, Bun, Volta, or Vite+ install), or
the CLI's own update command when T3 Code cannot tell. Claude, Codex, and
OpenCode installs T3 Code cannot identify stay manual: update them through the
installer you used. T3 Code runs `mise upgrade`
only for a tool your mise config requests as `latest` when the provider's binary
path is a mise shim or under the tool's `installs/<tool>/latest` link; update a
pinned version, or a path into one version's directory, through mise yourself.
Update a CLI installed with Nix through Nix.
Cursor and Antigravity update with T3 Code. Homebrew and Chocolatey installs
compare against the version their package manager offers, which can trail the
npm release; update Claude installed with Chocolatey through Chocolatey.

Add another provider instance for a separate account or configuration. Each
instance can have its own environment variables, such as API keys or a custom
base URL. Mark secret values as sensitive; after saving, T3 Code does not display
their original values.

For provider-specific setup and accounts, see [Codex](./providers-codex.md),
[Claude](./providers-claude.md), [OpenCode](./providers-opencode.md),
[Antigravity](./providers-antigravity.md), [Kiro](./providers-kiro.md),
[Pi](./providers-pi.md), [Muse Code](./providers-muse.md), and [fx](./providers-fx.md).

# Outside agents

Agents that T3 Code did not start can work with an environment through its MCP
server. They can read projects and threads, start and message threads, and
check which providers and models are available. This covers Claude Code or
Codex in your own terminal, ChatGPT, and bots that support MCP. Each agent signs
in once, and you choose what it may do.


## Approve a sign-in

The first time an agent connects, it opens a sign-in page. When the agent
reaches the environment through T3 Connect, the page opens on the T3 Code web
app: sign in with the T3 Connect account the environment is linked to and
approve there, without a code. Otherwise the page opens on the environment.
Either page names the agent and where its access goes:

- For an agent on your computer, approval returns to a `localhost` address on
  the computer that opened the page.
- For a hosted agent, approval goes to that service, such as `chatgpt.com`.
  Anyone who runs that service gets the access.

Only approve a sign-in you just started. On the environment's own page, enter a
code from **Use T3 Code in another app (MCP)**, **Settings → Sharing & access**,
or `t3 auth pairing create` on the host. A browser already signed in to the
environment with permission to manage access can approve without a code. On the
web app, **Use a sign-in code instead** opens the environment's own page.

A code from **Use T3 Code in another app (MCP)** already carries the level you
picked there. With another code, choose what the agent may do here: **Auto** is
selected by default, or the closest lower mode allowed by your organization’s
policy. Approving without a code starts at **Read only**:

- **Read only** lets the agent read projects and threads and see
  the available providers and models. It cannot change anything.
- **Supervised** through **Full access** also let it start, message and stop
  threads in every project. A thread it starts or steers cannot run with more
  permissions than the mode you chose.

row.description: Anti-AI-slop design skill for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.

documents.markdown:
# Hallmark **A design skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode that refuses to look AI-generated.** [usehallmark.com](https://www.usehallmark.com)  ·  fifty themes  ·  custom on request  ·  redesign and audit by name Made by Together AI.

Hallmark holds a hard floor and then gets out of the way. It deals three themes from a catalog of fifty materials, builds the page around what the visitor came to do, and lints the result in a real browser against the tells that read as machine-made: the eyebrow above every heading, tracked-capital labels, one coloured word in a headline, a page of empty frames or nothing but photographs, a hero that misses its screen, an email sign-up at the end of every page, a form that says thanks without sending anything. A fresh-context reviewer gets the last word. The gates come in tiers. The **Floor** never ships (contrast, focus, reduced motion, invented facts, a broken phone layout). **Reflex** gates are the defaults a model falls into; a build with a reason may overrule one on the record. **Finish** checks are craft detail that never blocks a ship. ## New in v2 - **Fifty themes.** Each is a material (paper, type, colour, surfaces, its own components and texture) with a picture of a finished page, and the build lays out its own page in it. - **Built from the job.** A booking page books, a shop sells, a newsletter subscribes: the action sits where the category puts it, and the page ends on it. - **Custom.** Ask for a custom page and Hallmark designs from your prompt alone, under the same rules and checks. - **Your real product.** Point it at a URL, a dev server or an app and it captures the screenshots itself. - **Real photographs.** 755 openly licensed photos, picked per subject and credited on the page. - **Redesign and audit.** `/hallmark redesign ` rebuilds a page and keeps its content and wiring; `/hallmark audit ` only reports. ## How a build runs 1. Pre-flight reads the project (fonts, palette, framework, a locked `design.md`) and asks once for the material: photos, screenshots, real numbers. Nothing is invented. 2. `scripts/theme.mjs deal` offers three themes that fit the prompt and clear the log; `draw` deals the page's anatomy from its job. 3. The hero is built alone, rendered and reviewed cold before the rest of the page exists. 4. `scripts/sloplint.mjs --render` checks the page at eight widths, then a subagent reviews it with fresh eyes. Each page is self-contained HTML and CSS, stamped in its first CSS comment with the decisions it took. ## Install ``` npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g ``` `-g` installs for every project; leave it off to install into the current one. Needs Node 18 or later. The browser checks (`sloplint --render`, screenshots) also need `npm i -g puppeteer-core` and Chrome; without them the static checks still run. | Harness | Lands in | Invoke | | --- | --- | --- | | Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/hallmark` | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | | Codex CLI | `~/.agents/skills/hallmark` | `$hallmark ` or describe a new build | | Cursor | finds the copies above | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | | OpenCode | finds the copies above | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | - **One harness only:** `npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g --agent claude-code` (or `codex`, `opencode`, `cursor`, `github-copilot`). - **As a Claude Code plugin:** `/plugin marketplace add nutlope/hallmark`, then `/plugin install hallmark@hallmark` (invoked as `/hallmark:hallmark`). - **From a clone:** `node skills/hallmark/scripts/install.mjs` validates every theme and reference before it copies; `install-hook.mjs` adds an edit-time Floor check to Claude Code. - **Lint any page:** `node skills/hallmark/scripts/sloplint.mjs --render`. - **If it does not fire on its own,** name it: *use hallmark to build ...*.

## Latest update (2026-10-15)

![Update overview](./docs/update-20261015.png)

- **Interpretation dataset v4.0 released**: 674,976 charts (every real solar date 1950–2026 × 12 double-hours × male/female) × 13 topics = 8,774,688 readings; 161 MB compressed, 56.6 GB uncompressed (v3.0: 33.1 GB), 77 per-year files plus an all-years bundle. See [Release v4.0-13d](https://github.com/Renhuai123/ziwei-doushu/releases/tag/v4.0-13d) and the dataset section below.
- **The 13 topics were revised sentence by sentence** against the verbatim transcripts of Ni Haixia's *Tian Ji* and the original *Complete Book*: untraceable citations removed or replaced with verbatim quotes (with episode and timestamp), sentences about impossible transformations removed, conditions spelled out, two-sided sentences resolved per chart, and health now follows Master Ni's whole-chart method instead of mapping stars to organs by Five Element. (The judgment library itself stays closed; the results are in the v4.0 dataset.)
- **Engine sync** ([PR #39](https://github.com/Renhuai123/ziwei-doushu/pull/39)): `chinaDSTSpan(year)` in `dst-cn.ts`; longitudes for province-administered county-level cities in `cities.ts`.
- **License**: `DATASET-LICENSE` now covers v4.0; quotations from *Tian Ji* inside the readings are not covered by the dataset license.

> **2026-11-08 addendum**: new public repo **[nishi-ziwei-video-reading](https://github.com/Renhuai123/nishi-ziwei-video-reading)**: reading all 1.6 million frames of the 17 *Tian Ji* Zi Wei episodes one by one with several large models. The plan, scripts, test results and mistakes are published as the work goes on; recent progress lives there.

> **2026-11-02 addendum**: the late Zi hour day change now uses **true solar time**, the same clock as the hour branch (#63). With a birthplace, 23:30 by the clock at 100°E (22:10 true solar time, the Hai hour) stays on the same day instead of becoming "Hai hour of the next day"; without a birthplace there is no correction and results are unchanged, matching ouranic.cn. An invalid leap-month policy now throws instead of silently charting as "same month" (#71). Thanks to Bortlesboat and xunguangzlj-cloud for the PRs and Verchiel666 for reviewing.

> **2026-10-31 addendum**: the live platform is now **OURANIC** and has moved from metisziwei.com to **[ouranic.cn](https://ouranic.cn/?from=gh-readme-en)**; old links redirect automatically. Code, datasets and licenses in this repo are unchanged.

> **2026-10-27 addendum**: engine sync. `true-solar-time.ts` accepts `utcOffsetMinutes` (the birthplace's standard UTC offset) for births outside China; results inside China are unchanged. New `clock-adjust.ts` converts a clock reading taken under daylight saving time (or an older time zone) to standard time; it never crosses midnight and is meant to run only when the user confirms. Correction: the engine detects China DST but has never subtracted it automatically; the table below said otherwise.


## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Renhuai123/ziwei-doushu.git
cd ziwei-doushu
npm ci
npm run dev          # charting demo at http://localhost:3000/chart

npm run typecheck    # TypeScript check
npm test             # charting regression tests
```

**No API key is needed for charting.** The open-source version contains **no backend routes**: AI interpretation (`/api/interpret`) and compatibility analysis (`/api/heming`) return 404 until you implement them yourself.

row.description: 🕷️ The BEST Web Scraping framework that handles everything from a single request to a full-scale crawl! Don't be shy, join here: https://discord.gg/EMgGbDceNQ and follow here for daily tips and tricks: https://x.com/Scrapling_dev

documents.markdown:
Effortless Web Scraping for the Modern Web





Selection methods · Fetchers · Spiders · Proxy Rotation · CLI · MCP

Scrapling is a Python Web Scraping framework that brings fast HTTP requests, stealth browsers, powerful parsing, and concurrent crawling into one library. Scrape static pages, render JavaScript, interact with websites, and extract data from the API calls behind them. Build crawlers with reusable sessions, proxy rotation, automatic retries, pause/resume, and built-in data exports. Use it from Python, the terminal, or your AI agent through its MCP server and Agent Skill. From extracting a few fields to collecting a whole website as clean Markdown, Scrapling covers the full scraping workflow. ## What you can do with Scrapling - **[Fetch & interact](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/fetching/choosing.html)**: Fast HTTP requests, stealth browsers, JavaScript rendering, Cloudflare Turnstile/Interstitial handling, persistent sessions, and background API capture. - **[Parse & extract](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/parsing/selection.html)**: CSS, XPath, text and regex search, adaptive element tracking, similar-element matching, and clean Markdown output. - **[Crawl & export](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/spiders/getting-started.html)**: Concurrent spiders, proxy rotation, retries, AutoThrottle, pause/resume, streaming, ready-made templates, and JSON/JSONL/CSV/XML exports. - **[Scrape with AI or from your terminal](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ai/mcp-server.html)**: An MCP server for AI agents to browse and extract data, an Agent Skill, CLI commands, and an interactive shell. Start with a single page: ```python from scrapling.fetchers import Fetcher page = Fetcher.get('https://quotes.toscrape.com/') quotes = page.css('.quote .text::text').getall() print(quotes) ``` Or scale up with a spider: ```python from scrapling.spiders import Spider, Response class QuotesSpider(Spider): name = "quotes" start_urls = ["https://quotes.toscrape.com/"] async def parse(self, response: Response): for quote in response.css('.quote'): yield { "text": quote.css('.text::text').get(), "author": quote.css('.author::text').get(), } result = QuotesSpider().start() print(len(result.items)) result.items.to_json("quotes.json") ``` This prints `10` and saves the quotes and authors to `quotes.json`.

### Advanced Websites Fetching with Session Support - **HTTP Requests**: Fast and stealthy HTTP requests with the `Fetcher` class. Can impersonate browsers' TLS fingerprint, headers, and use HTTP/3. - **Dynamic Loading**: Fetch dynamic websites with full browser automation through the `StealthyFetcher` class supporting Playwright's Chromium and Google's Chrome. - **Anti-bot Bypass**: Advanced stealth capabilities with `StealthyFetcher` and fingerprint spoofing. Can easily bypass all types of Cloudflare's Turnstile/Interstitial with automation. - **Session Management**: Persistent session support with `FetcherSession` and `StealthySession` classes for cookie and state management across requests. - **Proxy Rotation**: Built-in `ProxyRotator` with cyclic or custom rotation strategies across all session types, plus per-request proxy overrides. - **Domain & Ad Blocking**: Block requests to specific domains (and their subdomains) or enable built-in ad blocking (~3,500 known ad/tracker domains) in browser-based fetchers. - **DNS Leak Prevention**: Optional DNS-over-HTTPS support to route DNS queries through Cloudflare's DoH, preventing DNS leaks when using proxies. - **Remote Browsers**: Instead of launching a browser locally, connect to one that's already running through CDP with `cdp_url`, whether it's on the same machine, another host, or a managed browser provider. You can also point any browser fetcher at your own Chromium build with `executable_path`. - **Background API Capture**: Enable `record_requests=True` on a browser session, then search its saved responses with `session.network.search(limit=None)`. Read API data and HTTP errors across page loads without sending requests again. History is bounded and saves text response bodies. - **Async Support**: Complete async support across all fetchers and dedicated async session classes. ## Installation Scrapling requires Python 3.10 or higher: ```bash pip install scrapling ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > This installation only includes the parser engine and its dependencies, without any fetchers or commandline dependencies. So importing anything from `scrapling.fetchers` or `scrapling.spiders`, like in the examples above, will raise `ModuleNotFoundError` with this installation alone. If you are going to use any of the fetchers or spiders, install the fetchers' dependencies first as shown below. ### Optional Dependencies 1. If you are going to use any of the extra features below, the fetchers, or their classes, you will need to install fetchers' dependencies and their browser dependencies as follows: ```bash pip install "scrapling[fetchers]" scrapling install # normal install scrapling install --force # force reinstall ``` This downloads all browsers, along with their system dependencies and fingerprint manipulation dependencies. Or you can install them from the code instead of running a command like this: ```python from scrapling.cli import install install([], standalone_mode=False) # normal install install(["--force"], standalone_mode=False) # force reinstall ``` 2. Extra features: - Install the MCP server feature: ```bash pip install "scrapling[ai]" ``` - Install dependencies for ([building RAG systems](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ai/building-rag-systems.html)): ```bash pip install "scrapling[rag]" ``` - Install shell features (Web Scraping shell and the `extract` command): ```bash pip install "scrapling[shell]" ``` - Install everything: ```bash pip install "scrapling[all]" ``` Run `scrapling install` when you need browser fetchers. HTTP requests do not need a browser installation. ### Docker You can also install a Docker image with all extras and browsers with the following command from DockerHub: ```bash docker pull pyd4vinci/scrapling ``` Or download it from the GitHub registry: ```bash docker pull ghcr.io/d4vinci/scrapling:latest ``` This image is automatically built and pushed using GitHub Actions and the repository's main branch.

row.name: cloudflare/security-audit-skill
row.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings

documents.markdown:
# security-audit

A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.

This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in [Build your own vulnerability harness](https://blog.cloudflare.com/build-your-own-vulnerability-harness). The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.


## What it does

The skill runs a structured audit in six phases:

1. **Reconnaissance** -- map architecture, trust boundaries, input surfaces, prior evidence, and deterministic coverage in `architecture.md` and `coverage-ledger.json`.
2. **Coverage-led hunting** -- assign isolated hunters from ledger units, record their checks, and use coverage critics to find gaps.
3. **Candidate validation** -- give every unique candidate to a fresh verifier that tries to disprove it.
4. **Structured output** -- write `confirmed`, `needs_validation`, and `rejected` records to `findings.json` and validate them against `report-schema.json`.
5. **Independent record verification** -- fresh agents verify final source claims. Material replacements receive another independent verifier.
6. **Target-neutral reporting** -- derive `REPORT.md`, `FINDINGS-DETAIL.md`, and `NEEDS-VALIDATION.md` from the verified records and coverage ledger.

The parent runs `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs` after creating the ledger and after each later ledger update. It runs `validate-findings.cjs` in Phase 4 and again after every Phase 5 replacement.

The verdicts are distinct: `confirmed` has a complete source trace and bounded observed result, `needs_validation` has an exact unresolved fact and no severity, and `rejected` records a disproved candidate.

Multiple runs against the same repo are additive. The skill uses prior ledgers and findings to target gaps, revalidate changed source, and carry forward current-source evidence without treating stale or unresolved work as covered.


## Installation

Install the skill with the [Skills CLI](https://skills.sh):

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
  --skill security-audit
```

Use `--global` for a user-level installation:

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
  --skill security-audit \
  --global
```

Run `npx skills --help` for agent-selection and non-interactive options.


## Usage

Start your coding agent in (or pointed at) the codebase you want to audit, then ask it to do a security audit:

```
security audit this codebase
```

```
find security vulnerabilities in ./src
```

```
do a security review, output to ~/audits/my-project
```

The skill activates automatically when the request matches its trigger (security audit, find vulnerabilities, pen-test the code, etc.). A direct codebase audit or pen-test request uses full audit mode. Security questions and focused vulnerability work use guidance mode unless you request report artifacts. In full audit mode, an unspecified output directory defaults to `~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N>`. The workflow writes inside the target repository only when you explicitly select a directory that version control ignores.


## Requirements

- A coding agent with a model that supports tool use and parallel sub-agents
- Node.js for the zero-dependency findings and coverage-ledger validators
- An OS-enforced sandbox for target-controlled builds, tests, processes, browsers, emulators, fuzzers, and fixtures. It must disable external networking, use a sanitized allowlisted environment, enforce resource limits, and allow writes only to assigned scratch paths. Without these controls, the workflow keeps the lead as `needs_validation` instead of executing target code.

Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.

Studio | Quickstart | Showcase | Playground | Catalog | Docs | Discord

Download the desktop app: macOS · Windows · Linux (.deb)

HyperFrames is a free, open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. The [HyperFrames Studio app](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/studio-app) is free to use as well; its [Pro plan](https://hyperframes.studio/pricing) adds HeyGen's top video, image, voice and music models. Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent? Run `npx hyperframes skills update` once, then ask your agent to make a video. ### With an AI coding agent For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes ``` To enable auto-update for the **hyperframes** marketplace, run `claude` in a terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run `/plugin`, then select **Marketplaces** → **hyperframes** → **Enable auto-update**. Afterward, use `/hyperframes:hyperframes`. See the [plugin guide](docs/guides/plugins.mdx) for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration. For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use: ```bash npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes ``` > The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the **Core Skills** group is all you need; `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes` and `/figma` install on demand. Without the picker (a script or a CI job), `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly the core set, whereas `skills add --all` installs all 9 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under `.claude/skills` / `.agents/skills` are excluded by default. For the full published set use `npx hyperframes skills`. > > `skills add` resolves the skills.sh registry blob, which can lag `main` by hours. `npx hyperframes skills update` installs the skills from the release tag that matches your CLI version, so they match the CLI that runs them. Run project-local installs from your video project's directory. From a HyperFrames checkout, use `npx hyperframes skills update` for a global install instead: a project-local installer target can overlap the tracked `skills/` source and overwrite uncommitted edits. See [contributor setup](CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started). Try a prompt like: > Using `/hyperframes`, create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music. The skills teach agents the HyperFrames production loop: plan the video, write valid HTML, wire seekable animations, add media, lint, preview, and render. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, IBM Bob, and other coding agents that support skills. ## Skills HyperFrames ships 9 skills. Make any video by asking for it; the `/hyperframes` skill carries the contract and the references (film, captions, overlays, motion, look). Read it first. For standalone installation, default to the **core set** (`/hyperframes`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/media-use`, `/reverse-any-video`, `/style-sampling`). `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly that from anywhere; the interactive picker (`npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`) lists it as the "Core Skills" group, nothing pre-selected. The picker is interactive-only — a non-interactive or agent run without `--skill` installs all 9. Use `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --all` to install the complete published set deliberately (skips the picker), or `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --skill ` for just one (bare name, no leading `/`). Standalone installs stay lean after that: `npx hyperframes init` installs the **core set** only when it is missing and never touches a skill you already have (`npx hyperframes skills update` refreshes them, and never removes one); `/figma`, `/slideshow` and `/remotion-to-hyperframes` install **on demand** with `npx hyperframes skills update `. Nothing re-pulls the full set behind your back. ### Manually with the CLI ```bash npx hyperframes init my-video cd my-video npx hyperframes preview # preview in browser with live reload npx hyperframes render # render to MP4 ``` **Requirements:** Node.js 22+, FFmpeg ## How It Works Define a video as HTML. Add data attributes for timing and tracks. Use GSAP, CSS, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, WAAPI, or your own frame adapter for seekable animation. ```html

Launch day

``` Preview instantly in the browser. Render locally or in Docker. The renderer seeks each frame in headless Chrome and encodes the result with FFmpeg, so the same input produces the same video. ## HyperFrames Stack HyperFrames is the open-source rendering engine, plus a growing set of tools around HTML-native video creation. | Piece | Status | What it does | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | CLI | Available | Scaffold, preview, lint, inspect, and render local video projects | | Core / Engine / Producer | Available | Parse compositions, drive headless Chrome, encode video, and mix audio | | Catalog | Available | Reusable blocks and components for transitions, overlays, captions, charts, maps, and effects | | Agent skills | Available | Teach coding agents the video-production patterns that generic web docs miss | | Studio | Available, evolving | Browser surface for previewing and editing compositions | | AWS Lambda rendering | Available | Deploy a distributed render stack and drive renders from your laptop or CI | | [hyperframes.studio](https://hyperframes.studio/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme) | Available | Community playground for previewing, iterating, sharing, and rendering HTML-native video projects | | [frame.md](https://hyperframes.studio/design?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme) | Available | Invert your design system for the camera — a DESIGN.md superset an agent can compose video from | ## Why HyperFrames? - **HTML-native:** compositions are HTML files with data attributes. No React requirement, no proprietary timeline format. - **Agent-friendly:** agents already write HTML, and the CLI is non-interactive by default. - **Deterministic:** same input, same frames, same output. Built for CI, regression tests, and automated rendering. - **No build step:** an `index.html` composition plays as-is and can be previewed directly in the browser. - **Adapter-based animation:** bring GSAP, CSS animations, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, WAAPI, or a custom runtime. - **Open source:** Apache 2.0 license, with no per-render fees or commercial-use thresholds.

documents.markdown:
# Knowledge Work Plugins

Plugins that turn Claude into a specialist for your role, team, and company. Built for [Claude Cowork](https://claude.com/product/cowork), also compatible with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code).


## Why Plugins

Cowork lets you set the goal and Claude delivers finished, professional work. Plugins let you go further: tell Claude how you like work done, which tools and data to pull from, how to handle critical workflows, and what slash commands to expose — so your team gets better and more consistent outcomes.

Each plugin bundles the skills, connectors, slash commands, and sub-agents for a specific job function. Out of the box, they give Claude a strong starting point for helping anyone in that role. The real power comes when you customize them for your company — your tools, your terminology, your processes — so Claude works like it was built for your team.


## Plugin Marketplace

We're open-sourcing 11 plugins built and inspired by our own work:

| Plugin | How it helps | Connectors |
|--------|-------------|------------|
| **[productivity](./productivity)** | Manage tasks, calendars, daily workflows, and personal context so you spend less time repeating yourself. | Slack, Notion, Asana, Linear, Jira, Monday, ClickUp, Microsoft 365 |
| **[sales](./sales)** | Research prospects, prep for calls, review your pipeline, draft outreach, and build competitive battlecards. | Slack, HubSpot, Close, Clay, ZoomInfo, Notion, Jira, Fireflies, Microsoft 365 |
| **[customer-support](./customer-support)** | Triage tickets, draft responses, package escalations, research customer context, and turn resolved issues into knowledge base articles. | Slack, Intercom, HubSpot, Guru, Jira, Notion, Microsoft 365 |
| **[product-management](./product-management)** | Write specs, plan roadmaps, synthesize user research, keep stakeholders updated, and track the competitive landscape. | Slack, Linear, Asana, Monday, ClickUp, Jira, Notion, Figma, Amplitude, Pendo, Intercom, Fireflies |
| **[marketing](./marketing)** | Draft content, plan campaigns, enforce brand voice, brief on competitors, and report on performance across channels. | Slack, Canva, Figma, HubSpot, Amplitude, Notion, Ahrefs, SimilarWeb, Klaviyo |
| **[legal](./legal)** | Review contracts, triage NDAs, navigate compliance, assess risk, prep for meetings, and draft templated responses. | Slack, Box, Egnyte, Jira, Microsoft 365 |
| **[finance](./finance)** | Prep journal entries, reconcile accounts, generate financial statements, analyze variances, manage close, and support audits. | Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Slack, Microsoft 365 |
| **[data](./data)** | Query, visualize, and interpret datasets — write SQL, run statistical analysis, build dashboards, and validate your work before sharing. | Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Definite, Hex, Amplitude, Jira |
| **[enterprise-search](./enterprise-search)** | Find anything across email, chat, docs, and wikis — one query across all your company's tools. | Slack, Notion, Guru, Jira, Asana, Microsoft 365 |
| **[bio-research](./bio-research)** | Connect to preclinical research tools and databases (literature search, genomics analysis, target prioritization) to accelerate early-stage life sciences R&D. | PubMed, BioRender, bioRxiv, ClinicalTrials.gov, ChEMBL, Synapse, Wiley, Owkin, Open Targets, Benchling |
| **[cowork-plugin-management](./cowork-plugin-management)** | Create new plugins or customize existing ones for your organization's specific tools and workflows. | — |

Install these directly from Cowork, browse the full collection here on GitHub, or build your own.


## How Plugins Work

Every plugin follows the same structure:

```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json   # Manifest
├── .mcp.json                    # Tool connections
├── commands/                    # Slash commands you invoke explicitly
└── skills/                      # Domain knowledge Claude draws on automatically
```

- **Skills** encode the domain expertise, best practices, and step-by-step workflows Claude needs to give you useful help. Claude draws on them automatically when relevant.
- **Commands** are explicit actions you trigger (e.g., `/finance:reconciliation`, `/product-management:write-spec`).
- **Connectors** wire Claude to the external tools your role depends on — CRMs, project trackers, data warehouses, design tools, and more — via [MCP servers](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/).

Every component is file-based — markdown and JSON, no code, no infrastructure, no build steps.

## What It Does

This plugin gives you an AI-powered product management partner that can help with:

- **Feature Specs & PRDs** — Generate structured product requirements documents from a problem statement or feature idea. Includes user stories, requirements prioritization, success metrics, and scope management.
- **Roadmap Planning** — Create, update, and reprioritize your product roadmap. Supports Now/Next/Later, quarterly themes, and OKR-aligned formats with dependency mapping.
- **Stakeholder Updates** — Generate status updates tailored to your audience (executives, engineering, customers). Pulls context from connected tools to save you the weekly update grind.
- **User Research Synthesis** — Turn interview notes, survey data, and support tickets into structured insights. Identifies themes, builds personas, and surfaces opportunity areas with supporting evidence.
- **Competitive Analysis** — Research competitors and generate briefs with feature comparisons, positioning analysis, and strategic implications.
- **Metrics Review** — Analyze product metrics, identify trends, compare against targets, and surface actionable insights.
- **Product Brainstorming** — Explore problem spaces, generate ideas, and stress-test product thinking with a sharp sparring partner. Supports divergent ideation, assumption testing, and strategy exploration using frameworks like How Might We, Jobs-to-be-Done, First Principles, and Opportunity Solution Trees.


## Commands

| Command | What It Does |
|---|---|
| `/write-spec` | Write a feature spec or PRD from a problem statement |
| `/roadmap-update` | Update, create, or reprioritize your roadmap |
| `/stakeholder-update` | Generate a stakeholder update (weekly, monthly, launch) |
| `/synthesize-research` | Synthesize user research from interviews, surveys, and tickets |
| `/competitive-brief` | Create a competitive analysis brief |
| `/metrics-review` | Review and analyze product metrics |
| `/brainstorm` | Brainstorm a product idea, problem space, or strategic question with a thinking partner |


### Writing a PRD

```
You: /write-spec
Claude: What feature or problem are you speccing out?
You: We need to add SSO support for enterprise customers
Claude: [Asks about target users, constraints, success metrics]
Claude: [Generates full PRD with problem statement, user stories, requirements, success metrics, open questions]
```


## Data Sources

> If you see unfamiliar placeholders or need to check which tools are connected, see [CONNECTORS.md](CONNECTORS.md).

Connect your project management and communication tools for the best experience. Without them, provide context manually.

**Included MCP connections:**
- Chat (Slack) for team context and stakeholder threads
- Project tracker (Linear, Asana, monday.com, ClickUp, Atlassian) for roadmap integration, ticket context, and status tracking
- Knowledge base (Notion) for existing specs, research, and meeting notes
- Design (Figma) for design context and handoff
- Product analytics (Amplitude, Pendo) for usage data, metrics, and behavioral analysis
- User feedback (Intercom) for support tickets, feature requests, and user conversations
- Meeting transcription (Fireflies) for meeting notes and discussion context

**Additional options:**
- See [CONNECTORS.md](CONNECTORS.md) for alternative tools in each category

## What's new in 2.0

- **From 9 to 36 skills.** New skills cover deal reviews, close plans, stakeholder maps, renewals, customer health, lead routing, CRM updates, meeting booking, inbox sweeps and team pipeline views.
- **Works across CRMs and email providers.** Skills read your CRM's own stages and fields instead of assuming one vendor's setup, and work the same on Gmail or Outlook, Slack or Teams. No settings file is needed; a skill asks once for anything it cannot find.
- **Uses uploaded files when nothing is connected.** Upload a pipeline export, a transcript or a list of accounts, and the skill works from that.
- **Acts when you ask.** Skills can update CRM records, create email drafts or send email, post to chat and book meetings, within each connector's permissions. Changes a skill suggests on its own are shown to you first, with the evidence behind them.
- **Treats outside content as information.** Emails, call transcripts, chat messages and documents are read as information, never as instructions. If an email or transcript asks for an action, the skill shows you the action before anything happens.
- **Existing skill names still work.** `account-research`, `call-summary`, `forecast`, `call-prep`, `daily-briefing`, `draft-outreach`, `pipeline-review`, `competitive-intelligence` and `create-an-asset` keep their names, rebuilt on the new skills. Two behave differently: `create-an-asset` now builds decks, one-pagers and leave-behinds from your account data rather than landing pages or interactive demos, and `forecast` writes a commit, best-case and pipeline narrative instead of best, likely and worst scenarios.


## Skills

Skills run when your request matches, or directly by name (for example `/sales:call-summary`).


### After a call

```
/sales:call-summary
```

Paste your notes or transcript, or name the call if your call recorder is connected. You get a summary, a follow-up email draft, a team summary and proposed CRM updates. Nothing is written to the CRM or sent until you say so.

row.name: debpalash/VoiceStudio
row.description: VoiceStudio is the open-source, fully-local ElevenLabs alternative — voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription & audiobook creation in 646 languages.

documents.markdown:
## What you can do

Voice cloning
Turn a clean reference recording into speech in a familiar voice.
Video dubbing
Translate and dub videos with speech timed to the original.

Voice design
Describe a voice in words and generate it.
Local models
Choose your engines and download only the models you need.
More screenshots

Workspace overview
Model packs
- **Dictate & transcribe** — A floating dictation widget and local transcription - **Narrate & batch** — Stories, audiobooks and queued jobs - **Connect & automate** — Local API, MCP, reusable recipes and watch folders Start with **VoiceStudio** (default, powered by k2-fsa/OmniVoice), or pick from dozens of other engines in the Model Manager. See the [features & engine catalog](docs/feature-catalog.md).

## Platforms Experimental [Windows ROCm setup](docs/install/windows-rocm.md) supports selected RDNA 2 RX 6000 GPUs with targets `gfx1030`, `gfx1031` or `gfx1032`; RX 6500 XT (`gfx1034`) is excluded. GPU transcription uses a CTranslate2 build with native `gfx1031` kernels that this repository builds from upstream source and pins by hash, and setup checks actual GPU kernel execution. RX 6700 XT tests also cover native Torch speech generation and PyTorch Whisper. ROCm 10 faster-whisper uses a separate inference process to preserve safe CPU selection and fallback. Other cards and workloads retain the qualification limits in the guide. Performance presets validate changed engine selections in an offline child process before saving them, preserving fallback when an installed runtime fails. Choose your system, then expand an installation method. Native GGUF engines additionally support engine-specific Vulkan acceleration on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA GPUs ([OmniVoice](docs/engines/omnivoice-gguf.md#vulkan-acceleration), [CosyVoice](docs/engines/cosyvoice-gguf.md)). OmniVoice GGUF selects its GPU and model size automatically on Windows and Linux. Vulkan discovery retries a stalled hidden probe with a native summary; Windows and Linux desktop builds fail rather than silently ship without their Vulkan module.
macOS · Homebrew · DMG · installer
**Stable · Apple Silicon**
macOS 13.3+ · Apple Silicon: local engines with Metal (MPS). ```sh brew tap debpalash/tap brew trust --cask debpalash/tap/voicestudio brew install --cask debpalash/tap/voicestudio ```
DMG Download the DMG for your Mac, open it and drag VoiceStudio into Applications. [Download](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) · [Guide](docs/install/macos.md)
One-command installer ```sh curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh ```
Intel Mac · remote backend · Limited The app UI runs on Intel; connect it to a VoiceStudio backend on another computer. [Guide](docs/install/macos.md)
> [!NOTE] > On macOS, "VoiceStudio is damaged and can't be opened" means Gatekeeper blocked the app, not that the download is broken. See the [Gatekeeper fix](docs/install/macos.md#gatekeeper-quarantine).
Windows · PowerShell · EXE
**Stable · x64**
Windows 10/11 x64 · NVIDIA CUDA · AMD ROCm (opt-in) · CPU. ```powershell irm https://voicestudio.sh/install.ps1 | iex ``` [Download the Windows installer](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) · [Guide](docs/install/windows.md) · [AMD ROCm](docs/install/windows-rocm.md)
Windows on ARM · experimental Native app UI; the x64 Python backend runs under emulation on the CPU. [Download](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) · [Guide](docs/install/windows.md)
Linux · AUR · Snap · DEB · AppImage · Nix
**Stable · x64**
Linux x64 · NVIDIA CUDA · CPU · Vulkan for supported GGUF engines.
One-command installer ```sh curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh ```
Arch / Manjaro / EndeavourOS · AUR ```sh yay -S voicestudio-bin ``` Also available through `paru -S voicestudio-bin`. [Development sources](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/voicestudio-git) · `yay -S voicestudio-git`
Build from AUR and install with pacman ```sh sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel git git clone https://aur.archlinux.org/voicestudio-bin.git cd voicestudio-bin makepkg -s sudo pacman -U ./voicestudio-bin-*.pkg.tar.zst ```
Ubuntu / Debian / Linux Mint · DEB Download the `.deb` into the current folder, then install it: [Download](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) ```sh sudo apt install ./VoiceStudio-*-linux-x64.deb ```
Snap · Ubuntu, Fedora, openSUSE and more With [snapd installed](https://snapcraft.io/docs/installing-snapd): ```sh sudo snap install voicestudio ``` To enable microphone access: ```sh sudo snap connect voicestudio:audio-record ```
Any Linux distribution · AppImage Download the AppImage into the current folder, then launch it: [Download](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) ```sh chmod +x VoiceStudio-*-linux-x64.AppImage ./VoiceStudio-*-linux-x64.AppImage ```
Nix / NixOS · source environment Enter the repository’s FHS development environment, then run from source: ```sh git clone https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio.git cd VoiceStudio nix develop .#fhs bun run dev ``` [Guide](docs/install/nix.md)
[Guide](docs/install/linux.md)
Docker · GHCR · Docker Hub
Stable images · CPU · NVIDIA CUDA · AMD ROCm. **Run locally on the CPU (Bash)** ```sh export OMNIVOICE_API_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" docker run -d --name omnivoice \ -p 127.0.0.1:3900:3900 \ -e OMNIVOICE_API_KEY \ -e OMNIVOICE_DATA_DIR=/app/omnivoice_data \ -v omnivoice-data:/app/omnivoice_data \ ghcr.io/debpalash/voicestudio:stable printf 'API key: %s\n' "$OMNIVOICE_API_KEY" ``` Open http://localhost:3900 and use the API key printed below. [NVIDIA, AMD ROCm and Compose instructions](docs/install/docker.md) [Docker Hub mirror](https://hub.docker.com/r/palashdeb/omnivoice-studio): `palashdeb/omnivoice-studio:stable`
Android · APK · Obtainium · F-Droid repository
Android 10+ · Preview · On-device, offline after model download. [Download APK](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) · [Guide](docs/mobile.md#install)
F-Droid · VoiceStudio repository Add this repository in an F-Droid-compatible client; verify the fingerprint in the guide. ```text https://debpalash.github.io/VoiceStudio/fdroid/repo ``` [Guide](store/fdroid/README.md)
Obtainium · GitHub releases Add this source in Obtainium, or import the provided configuration. ```text https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio ``` [Import configuration](https://debpalash.github.io/VoiceStudio/obtainium.json)
Install over USB with adb ```sh adb install -r VoiceStudio-*-android.apk ```
iPhone / iPad · IPA · sideloading
iOS / iPadOS 17+ · Preview · On-device, offline after model download. Download the IPA and follow the signing and sideloading instructions. [Download](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) · [Guide](docs/mobile.md#install)
Desktop and phone installers are on the [latest release](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest); Docker images come from GHCR. No GPU? The app is fully usable on the CPU, just slower. Native GGUF engines can also use Vulkan on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA GPUs; OmniVoice GGUF picks its GPU and model size automatically on Windows and Linux ([OmniVoice](docs/engines/omnivoice-gguf.md#vulkan-acceleration), [CosyVoice](docs/engines/cosyvoice-gguf.md)). Speed by engine and hardware: [performance](docs/performance.md).

# VoiceStudio — Install on macOS

VoiceStudio's macOS desktop app is built with Electron. The archived Tauri app
is no longer maintained; if you still run it, follow the
[migration guide](../electron-migration.md).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Intel Macs are not supported** for the local backend (app UI only).
> PyTorch stopped shipping Intel-Mac (macOS
> x86_64) wheels after 2.2.x and VoiceStudio's dependencies need a newer torch,
> so a local Python backend cannot install on an Intel Mac — from the DMG *or*
> from source ([#889](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/issues/889)).
> On Intel, packaged setup stops before creating a Python environment or
> downloading dependencies and shows remote-backend guidance instead: use the
> remote connection controls on the setup screen to point the app at a backend
> on another machine, or run VoiceStudio on an Apple Silicon Mac, Windows, or
> Linux. A source checkout behaves the same way: `bun run setup:api` stops
> before syncing anything, and the app opens the same remote-backend screen
> instead of reporting an incomplete Python environment
> ([#3584](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/issues/3584)).


## Building from source

Use this for development or to run current `main`. To build and install a
desktop package from `main` without a checkout, use the shell installer's
[`--main` mode](script.md#building-main). Local source builds are not
local-backend capable on Intel Macs either.

Prerequisites (use a native arm64 terminal on Apple Silicon):

- **Xcode Command Line Tools** — `xcode-select --install` (includes **git**
  and the C toolchain; `curl` ships with macOS).
- **Bun** — `curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash`.
- **uv** — `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` (it provides the
  managed Python 3.11 the backend uses).
- **Node.js 22.12.0 or newer** and **Rust / Cargo** (`brew install rust`, or rustup —
  reopen the terminal or source `"$HOME/.cargo/env"` afterwards) for the
  Electron native helper.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio.git
cd VoiceStudio
node electron/scripts/node-version.mjs
```

If the Node check fails, stop here, upgrade Node.js, and reopen your terminal
before continuing. Then install dependencies and prepare the local backend
(skip API setup when using an external backend or an Intel Mac):

```bash
bun install
bun run setup:api   # create the Python environment with uv
bun run dev         # Electron with hot reload; it starts and supervises the backend
```

Use `bun run desktop-prod` to build and launch the production bundle, or
`bun run dist` to create local DMG/zip packages in `electron/release/` without
publishing. Local packages are unsigned. See
[Electron setup](../../electron/README.md) for backend configuration.

row.name: pbakaus/impeccable
row.description: The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder, review with critique and audit, catch AI slop before it ships.

documents.markdown:
# Impeccable The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with `polish` and `bolder`, review with `critique` and `audit`, and catch AI slop before it ships. From your project root: ```bash npx impeccable install ``` Reload your coding tool, then run `/impeccable init` in your agent (`$impeccable init` on Codex). Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). | Without Impeccable | With Impeccable | |---|---| | ![Villa Castagneto built without Impeccable: cream background, a thin serif headline with an italic accent, two pill buttons, and flat vector illustrations in rounded cards](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-without.webp) | ![Villa Castagneto built with Impeccable: a full-bleed engraved night scene of the villa on its cliff above the sea, a condensed cream and vermilion headline, and a month strip along the bottom](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-with.webp) | Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water. For a full project, see the [Neo Mirai case study](https://impeccable.style/cases/neo-mirai): a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page. ## Why Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects. - **Words for what you want.** "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. `/impeccable bolder the pricing cards` loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target. - **A reviewer.** `critique` scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. `audit` checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish). - **A slop detector.** 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key. Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see [Build something new](https://impeccable.style/docs/new-work) for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component: ``` /impeccable critique the pricing cards ``` ## How it works Run `/impeccable init` once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes `PRODUCT.md`. Every later command reads it. Run `/impeccable document` to capture your existing visual system in `DESIGN.md`, so changes stay on-brand. [More on context files](https://impeccable.style/docs/context). Then name a command and a target: ``` /impeccable critique the onboarding flow /impeccable quieter the landing page /impeccable polish settings /impeccable harden checkout ``` Or just describe what you want: `/impeccable redo this hero section`. Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with `/impeccable pin audit` to get `/audit` as its own shortcut. ### Live mode `/impeccable live` opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. [Iterate in the browser](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/iterate-live). Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your `package.json`'s optional `impeccable:manual-edit-validate` script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo. Apply sends staged copy edits to your chat agent while a live session is polling. If none has polled in the last minute, it runs the `codex` CLI from your PATH instead (or `claude` when codex is missing), with approvals, permission checks, and sandboxing off (`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` or `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`) and your environment inherited. Its prompt carries the staged edits, the edited elements' HTML and nearby text, the page URL, and candidate source paths. Set `IMPECCABLE_LIVE_COPY_AGENT=chat` in the environment that starts live mode to keep Apply in your chat session, or `off` to disable Apply. The server reads it once at startup. ## Installation ```bash npx impeccable install ``` The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. `npx impeccable update` refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass `--providers=claude,codex,cursor` and `--scope=project|global`. Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open `/hooks` and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run `/hooks-trust` or launch with `--trust`. In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run `hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook` once. [Allow the hook in your harness](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks#allow-the-hook-in-your-harness). Node is only needed for `npx`. The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into `~/.impeccable/bin/`.
Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins **Claude Code:** `/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable`, then open `/plugin` and install Impeccable. **GitHub Copilot in VS Code:** install [Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=renaissance-geek.impeccable) or run `code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable`. Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. [Details](docs/VSCODE-EXTENSION.md). **Grok Build:** `grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust` installs the skill, agents, and hook.
Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team) ```bash git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor ``` Commit `.gitmodules`, the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. To upgrade, run `git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable`, rerun the `link` command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass `--force`.
Manual copy, no Node required Download the ZIP for your tool from [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style), or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy `skills/impeccable` from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder. | Tool | Repo folder | Global skills folder | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `.claude/` | `~/.claude/skills/` | | Cursor | `.cursor/` | | | Codex CLI, Replit Agent | `.agents/` | `~/.agents/skills/` | | Devin | `.devin/` | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/` | | GitHub Copilot | `.github/` | | | Gemini CLI | `.gemini/` | | | Google Antigravity | `.agent/` | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | | OpenCode | `.opencode/` | | | Grok Build | `.grok/` | `~/.grok/skills/` | | Hermes Agent | `.hermes/` | `${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/` | | DeepSeek Harness | `.dsh/` | `${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/` | | Pi | `.pi/` | | | Qoder | `.qoder/` | `~/.qoder/skills/` | | Rovo Dev | `.rovodev/` | `~/.rovodev/skills/` | | Mistral Vibe | `.vibe/` | `~/.vibe/skills/` | | Trae | `.trae/` | `~/.trae/skills/` | | Trae China | `.trae-cn/` | `~/.trae-cn/skills/` | For example: `mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/`. Notes: - A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run `npx impeccable install` to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path. - OpenCode also needs `.opencode/commands/impeccable.md` copied into your project's `.opencode/commands/` to provide `/impeccable`. - Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run `hermes skills trust` from the project root. Global installs need no trust step. - Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/context/skills) and [Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/) skills docs. - Restart Trae after copying. - `impeccable install` and `update` manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when `DSH_HOME` is inside your home directory.

Run systematic **technical** quality checks and generate a comprehensive report. Don't fix issues; document them for other commands to address.

This is a code-level audit, not a design critique. Check what's measurable and verifiable in the implementation.

**Web only.** Native platforms (`ios` / `android` / `adaptive`) route to [audit.native.md](audit.native.md) instead; if the project is native, switch to it now.


### Audit Health Score

| # | Dimension | Score | Key Finding |
|---|-----------|-------|-------------|
| 1 | Accessibility | ? | [most critical a11y issue or "--"] |
| 2 | Performance | ? | |
| 3 | Theming | ? | |
| 4 | Responsive Design | ? | |
| 5 | Implementation Integrity | ? | |
| **Total** | | **??/20** | **[Rating band]** |

**Rating bands**: 18-20 Excellent (minor polish), 14-17 Good (address weak dimensions), 10-13 Acceptable (significant work needed), 6-9 Poor (major overhaul), 0-5 Critical (fundamental issues)


### Executive Summary
- Audit Health Score: **??/20** ([rating band])
- Total issues found (count by severity: P0/P1/P2/P3)
- Top 3-5 critical issues
- Recommended next steps

### Purpose

Resolve one stable target, run two independent assessments, synthesize a design critique, persist a snapshot, and ask the user what to improve next. The chat response is the primary deliverable; the snapshot is an archive of that run.


### Hard Invariants

- Assessment A (design review) and Assessment B (detector/browser evidence) are both required, except on a native platform (see Assessment Orchestration).
- Assessment A and B MUST run as two isolated sub-agents whenever a sub-agent/Task tool is exposed. Running them inline in this context is "possible" but is NOT permitted; it is a degraded run. Inline is allowed ONLY when no sub-agent tool exists (or the user declined, on harnesses that ask). Native platforms run A alone (see Assessment Orchestration).
- If you degrade for any reason, the report's first line MUST be a banner: `⚠️ DEGRADED: single-context (<reason>)`. A silent degraded critique is a failed critique.
- Assessment A must finish before detector findings enter the parent synthesis context. Detector output is deterministic, but it still anchors judgment.
- A skipped detector is a failed critique run unless `impeccable detect` is missing or crashes after a real attempt, or the platform is native (see Assessment Orchestration).
- Viewable targets require browser inspection when available.
- Any local server started only for critique visualization must run in the background, have a recorded stop method, and be stopped before final reporting unless the user asks to keep it.
- Do not claim a user-visible overlay exists unless script injection succeeded and the detector ran in the page.
- The question is the LAST thing in the response. Write the entire report out first, then ask; nothing follows the question. Prose emitted after a structured question is withheld until the user answers it, so a report written after the question reads as if the critique never ran.
- A run that ends with neither the targeted questions nor a literal `Questions skipped: <reason>` line is an incomplete run. The report is not the finish; the close is.


### Setup

1. **Resolve the target** to a concrete file path or URL. Prefer a source path over a dev-server URL when both identify the same surface; ports drift, paths do not.
   - "the homepage" -> `site/pages/index.astro` or `index.html`
   - "the settings modal" -> the primary component file
   - "this page" -> the current URL or source file
2. **Confirm the target slugs cleanly**:
   ```bash
   {{scripts_path}}/impeccable critique-storage slug "<resolved-path-or-url>"
   ```
   Every later command also accepts the resolved target directly and derives the same slug internally; never hand-write a slug. If this exits non-zero, skip persistence and trend for this run, but continue the critique.
3. **Read `.impeccable/critique/ignore.md`** if it exists. Drop matching findings silently; it is the only prior-run input critique consumes.
